Initial 50-60 stage/R=3 columns were far too sloppy: root tops contained 17% C5 and deC3 cuts were badly contaminated. All three products were unsellable and cost was $384M/yr. Try fewer stages but higher R/B=4-5 and no pressure drop to warm condensers and improve volatility/cost tradeoff. Target TT=C3 blend, TB=C4 blend, BT=C5 blend; then extend BB.

note: Raise driving force substantially on the three blend-cutting columns to cross 95% specifications and establish positive revenue.

Current test raises R to 8 and root boil-up to 10, with 50-60 stages. Target TT=C3 blend, TB=C4 blend, BT=C5 blend. If revenue appears, extend BB into C6 paraffin blend and heavies; otherwise reduce scope/cost.

PLAN: Build a four-column blend train: root C4-/C5+, top C3/C4 blends, bottom C5/C6+, then C6 paraffin blend/heavies. Tune duties down after establishing sales; prune marginal columns.
Current 90/12 root actually split C5/C6+, so T split C4-/C5 and left TT an unsaleable C3/C4 mixture. C6 paraffin blend earned $1096M/yr, proving that product is valuable. Costs at 75-90 stages and R/B=10-12 were prohibitive ($1366M/yr for only 3 columns). Restructure now with moderate 50-70 stages and R/B=4-8. Expected blend revenues roughly C3 $88M, C4 $186M, C5 $618M, C6 paraffin $1096M. Leave heavies unsold initially. If purities miss, identify the limiting adjacent key pair and adjust only that column.

Current four columns all lose valuable light key into bottoms: TB has 21% C4, BT has 13% C5 from root leakage plus poor root cut, and BB retains much N-hexane. Symmetric R=B=12 did not fix this. Test much higher boil-up with moderate reflux to strip light keys upward. Root must keep C5 out of B; B cannot remove C5 from its own tops. TT can never meet C3 95% because ethane stays with C3; its value is C4 bottoms only. Target C4 $126M+, C5 ~$497M, paraffin ~$1059M. Once specs crossed, reduce cost aggressively.

PLAN: Replace the poor C5/C6 root with the easy C4/C5 root; T removes C3-/ethane to sell C4, B splits C5 from C6+, and BB sells C6 paraffin over heavies. Measure leakage, then sharpen only failing cuts and finally reduce cost.
The current C5/C6 root is intrinsically expensive and contaminates every downstream product. New root should isolate C4- (774 mol/s) from C5+ (2526): TB is C4 blend (~$126M), BT C5 blend (~$497M), BBT C6-paraffin (~$1059M). TT is discarded as unsellable ethane/C3. Moderate duties should avoid prior excessive costs; pressure drops keep condensers warmer. C3 recovery is deferred because ethane requires another split.
